load.title: Seat the rotor upright
load.instruction: Grip the rotor in the tray, carry it upright over the spindle, and release to seat it. If it is already seated, leave it in place.
load.science: Unbalance is mass times radius. Its rotating force grows with the square of speed. We will measure that response, calculate a correction, and test it.

home.title: Reference the vibration probe
home.instruction: With the rotor loaded and stopped, press the physical Home button. Confirm the probe reads six millimeters. Press Home now, even if an earlier reference is displayed.
home.science: A repeatable sensor position makes the calibration meaningful. Homing or changing probe position, speed, or mode discards the previous calibration.

guard.title: Latch the enclosure
guard.instruction: Grip the orange handle, lower the guard fully, then release. Check that the interlock says closed, and let go of every fixture handle.
guard.science: The interlock inhibits starting until the guard is closed and the controls are released. This does not certify real machinery containment.

baseline.title: Measure the baseline
baseline.instruction: Press Baseline on the station. Keep the guard closed, and wait for capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero. Stop aborts an incomplete capture.
baseline.science: This is the reference vibration before the trial mass. Displacement is in micrometers peak. For a sine wave, divide peak by the square root of two to get root mean square amplitude.

open_trial.title: Open for the known trial
open_trial.instruction: Once the spindle reads zero, grip the orange handle and lift the guard. Leave the baseline setup unchanged until the known trial is installed.
open_trial.science: Baseline and trial must use the same speed, correction radius, and sensor setup. Otherwise their difference would mix the trial effect with a changed measurement system.

trial_fit.title: Install the known trial
trial_fit.instruction: With the guard open and plane A selected, press Fit Trial on the station. The helper adds a known quarter-gram trial relative to the baseline.
trial_fit.science: This known change reveals how unbalance affects vibration. Keeping the other plane at its baseline makes the calibration change independent.

close_trial.title: Latch for Trial A
close_trial.instruction: Lower the orange guard handle fully, release your grip, and check closed. Keep the trial mass installed for the next measurement.
close_trial.science: Closing the guard prepares the apparatus; it does not measure anything. The trial capture must observe the known mass at exactly the baseline setup and speed.

trial_measure.title: Measure Trial A
trial_measure.instruction: Press Measure Trial A on the station. Wait for the new capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero. An old trial result cannot replace this measurement.
trial_measure.science: Subtracting the baseline response isolates the known trial's effect. Tachometer-referenced analysis separates the once-per-revolution response from offset and second-harmonic motion.

solve.title: Calculate the correction
solve.instruction: At zero speed, press Solve. Read the calculated correction mass, angle, and condition information on the analyzer. Rejected trial data must be measured again.
solve.science: The influence coefficient, alpha, is the response change divided by trial unbalance. Correction is minus the baseline response divided by alpha. This accounts for support phase, rather than guessing the heavy spot.

open_apply.title: Open for correction
open_apply.instruction: At zero speed, lift the orange guard handle. Keep the calculated solution available. Do not change probe geometry or test speed.
open_apply.science: The correction depends on the calibrated response of the apparatus. Changing the sensor or support can invalidate that sensitivity, even if a displayed mass still looks plausible.

apply.title: Install the calculated correction
apply.instruction: With the guard open, press Apply Correction on the station. The helper removes the trial configuration and installs the total calculated masses.
apply.science: The correction is added to the baseline mass vector, not to the temporary trial mass. This is still a prediction; a new measurement must test it.

close_verify.title: Latch for verification
close_verify.instruction: Lower the guard fully and release the handle. Keep the calculated correction installed, and confirm closed before measuring.
close_verify.science: Single-plane correction targets sensor A at one speed. Sensor B can still show vibration. Only a fresh measurement can tell us whether the installed correction works.

verify.title: Verify with a fresh measurement
verify.instruction: Press Verify on the station. Wait through analysis and coast-down to zero, then inspect the measured reduction. A low reduction is a result to diagnose and retry.
verify.science: Fresh verification tests the installed correction. Old results or changed settings do not count. Near zero amplitude, phase becomes unobservable, rather than a useful correction direction.

repeat.title: Check repeatability
repeat.instruction: Press Repeat with the setup unchanged. Wait for all three measurement windows and coast-down. Read the mean amplitude, standard deviation, and Type A standard error.
repeat.science: Standard deviation describes scatter. Dividing it by the square root of three gives the standard error of the mean. These simulated repeats do not measure calibration bias or total uncertainty.

report.title: Save the evidence
report.instruction: Press Save Report on the station and confirm the saved path. The guide finishes after the success message, while your laboratory data stay available.
report.science: The report links settings, accepted measurements, calculations, events, and limits. Keep it as evidence of this synthetic exercise. Guide completion can include skips; it does not certify competence or equipment safety.
